correctness.rationale: For n=4k+3, a=n^2,b=(n+1)^2,c=(n+2)^2, reduction identities create complete Apéry reps q b+r c with top q=0..L and lower r=1..k, q=0..L-1, L=4(n-1), giving exactly a distinct residues. Under t=q-Lr, x(t)=alpha*t mod a and alpha*(2n-1)=4a-1, exact gap heights h=q+9r+floor(alpha*t/a) identify only 2n-2 top-row cells each contributing 7(k+1) isolated gaps and k(2n-3) lower cells each contributing 2n+2. Their sum is n^3+1. Independently computed shortest-path Apéry representatives and neighbor gap counts for n=3,7,11,15,19,23,27, all matching the cubic.
residual_risks: Only n>=3 congruent 3 mod 4. At n=3 the third generator is redundant; proof explicitly covers k=0. Dijkstra tests are finite, not an infinite proof.
